changelog.summary: Agenda: a new calendar button in the header opens Coming up, a list of days and times found in notes, soonest first, grouped by day (Today, Tomorrow, In 5 days…), with the time in the margin ('all day' when there is none) and the date words underlined in red pencil. Found on the phone by plain rules: today/tonight/tomorrow, weekday names (this/next/on Friday; 'next Friday' means the Friday of the following week), '12 Nov', 'Nov 12th', '12/11' (day first, only after words like 'on'/'due' or at the start of a line), '12/11/26', '2026-11-12', 'the 1st', 'in 3 days/two weeks/a fortnight', 'this weekend', and times such as 3pm, 3:30 pm, 15:30 and noon. Words are read from the note's own page date. Ticked to-dos drop off; addresses, phone numbers and prices aren't mistaken for dates; a time with no date on the note's own day only counts if it's still ahead. Tapping an item opens its note; tapping a day heading opens that day. Every day page now shows a 'Planned for today / this day' slip listing notes from other days that point at it. 'Show the last two weeks' reveals recent past items. No schema change.

Smart collections: the search page, with the box empty, opens on a contents page of ten collections with counts: To-dos (notes with boxes still to tick), Links, Photos, Voice notes, Pinned, Addresses, Phone numbers, Emails, Money and Ideas. Notes are sorted on the phone by plain rules (patterns for web addresses, Australian and international phone numbers, $/A$/€/£ amounts, street addresses with Australian states and postcodes, idea phrases such as 'Idea:', 'what if', 'would be cool if', #idea), with no folders and no AI. Inside a collection, what was found is marked in each note, and links, numbers, emails and addresses get small Open / Call / Email / Maps chips (Apple Maps links for addresses; nothing is sent unless the person taps). Typing switches back to normal search. No schema change.

Voice notes: with the note box empty, a microphone takes the Add button's place; tapping it opens a recording panel with a timer and level meter, Stop and save, and Cancel (asks before throwing away more than 5 seconds). Recordings are made with MediaRecorder (AAC/MP4 on iPhone), kept as Blobs in IndexedDB on the phone, and play back on the page with a seek bar, elapsed time and 1x/1.5x/2x speed. Leaving the app, an interruption or the one-hour limit stops and keeps what was recorded; the screen is kept awake while recording where the iPhone allows it. Captions work like photo captions and are searchable; recordings can be saved through the share sheet from the editor; delete has Undo; backups and restore include recordings, and the restore summary counts them. Transcription: the iPhone keyboard's dictation mic is recommended in Writing tips; browser speech recognition is not offered because it couldn't be verified on a real iPhone and may send audio to Apple. No schema change (recordings share the v2 media store).

Checklists, pins and tags: a to-do button in the note box (and in the editor) turns a line into a tick box, Return starts the next to-do and Return on an empty one ends the list; boxes tick right on the page with a done count in the margin and a small 'All done' when the last one is ticked. Notes can be pinned to the top of their day from the editor (with Undo), shown with a pin on the margin rule and a dashed rule under the pinned group. Words starting with # become tag chips; tapping one searches for it, and the empty search page lists every tag with counts. To-dos live in the note text as [ ] / [x] lines and pins as an extra field, so search, backups and older versions keep working. No schema change. Writing tips added to Settings.

Find anything: a search page that looks for every word typed (any order, ignoring case and accents) across notes and photo captions, results grouped by day with matches highlighted and photo thumbnails, tap a result to open that day at the note. Looking back (a week ago, a month ago, this date in earlier years) shows when the search box is empty, and an On this day slip appears on today's page when earlier years have notes on this date. No schema change.

Photo notes: camera or library from the capture bar (several at once), shrunk and re-saved on the phone without hidden metadata, thumbnails sized to the ruled lines, full-screen view with pinch/double-tap zoom, swipe between photos and Save via the share sheet, optional captions, delete with undo, photos included in encrypted backups and restore. Schema v2 adds a media store (additive migration from v1).

Foundation: install screen, ruled day pages with timestamped notes, quick capture, edit and delete with undo, day flipping, date picker, offline service worker with update prompt, persistent storage request, CSP lockdown, encrypted backup and restore.

knownIssues: Tested in headless Chromium only; not yet confirmed on a real iPhone (Safari/WebKit).
The quick-capture bar lifts above the iOS keyboard using visualViewport; behaviour on the real keyboard is unverified.
Backups use the iOS share sheet (Save to Files); the download fallback is untested on iOS.
Backups are built in memory in one piece; with many hundreds of photos this may hit iPhone memory limits. Chunked backups may be needed later.
Photo picking, camera capture, HEIC handling and pinch zoom are untested on a real iPhone.
Search, On this day and the highlighter marks are tested in headless Chromium only; the iOS keyboard's Search key and focus behaviour are unverified on a real iPhone.

The to-do button is meant to keep the iOS keyboard up, and Return is meant to continue a list; both rely on iOS Safari key and pointer events that are unverified on a real iPhone. Tick boxes are 28 px tall (one ruled line), below Apple's 44 px guideline, though 42 px wide.

Voice recording and playback are tested in headless Chromium with a fake microphone (WebM/Opus) only. On iPhone, MediaRecorder should produce AAC in MP4; recording, seeking, the microphone permission prompt (iOS may ask again each launch of a home-screen app), the wake lock and the orange-dot behaviour are unverified on a real device.

Browser speech recognition (live transcription) is deliberately not offered: it couldn't be verified on a real iPhone, may not work in home-screen apps, and Apple may process the audio on its servers.

Collection rules are tuned for Australian formats (phone numbers, states, postcodes) and English phrasing; they will miss some addresses and ideas and may occasionally pick up something that isn't one. Collections are tested in headless Chromium only; how iOS opens tel:, mailto:, Apple Maps and outside links from a home-screen app is unverified on a real iPhone.

Agenda rules are English-only and day-first (Australian) for numeric dates; they will miss some phrasings (e.g. 'next week', 'end of the month', time ranges keep only the first time) and can occasionally read a casual weekday mention ('I loved Friday') as a plan. 'Next Friday' is read as the Friday of the following week. Items can't be dismissed one by one; tick the to-do or edit the note. Tested in headless Chromium only.
nextUp: Stage 8: Places: attach the current location to a note (only when tapped, stored only on the phone) or type an address; a Places list with Open in Apple Maps links; no map tiles.
